sam: Heads-up: Acme POC is failing when clients talk to our private endpoint. They get TLS handshake errors and our client library times out. Can infra/sales triage?

elaine: Which error codes do they see? Region/VPC?

sam: Region is eu-central-1. Client logs: `TLS alert handshake failure` then `deadline exceeded` after ~10s. Gateway logs show occasional 495-like upstream TLS failures and repeated OCSP fetch attempts timing out.

josh: Do we have any server-side TLS alerts? Any `unable to get local issuer` lines?

sam: Support log snippet: 
```
2026-02-21T09:22:03Z outbound: dial tcp 10.200.7.8:80: i/o timeout
2026-02-21T09:22:03Z tls: certificate verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2026-02-21T09:22:03Z ocsp: fetch failed: dial tcp 10.200.7.8:80: connection refused
```

lee: That looks like split-horizon DNS: our CA's OCSP responder `ocsp.globalca.net` is resolving to RFC1918 for them. Their VPC firewall blocks egress to that CIDR.

josh: Ask them to run these from the pod/host that makes outbound calls: 
1) `dig +short ocsp.globalca.net @<their-resolver>`
2) `curl -v http://ocsp.globalca.net/`
3) `openssl s_client -connect ocsp.globalca.net:80 -status -servername ocsp.globalca.net`
Explain they'll need to run from the same node/container as our connector.

sam: Also ask them to check whether they have an internal OCSP mirror or firewall rule that rewrites public OCSP names to internal appliances. We've seen middleboxes doing that and returning unreachable IPs to third-party services.

elaine: From a short-term mitigation POV we can offer: 1) provide a short-term private deployment trial so our service runs inside their VPC with allowed egress, 2) support a temporary client flag that bypasses OCSP for the POC (security signoff required), 3) they add an egress rule to allow the OCSP responder's published IPs.

procurement: On pricing: Private deployment trial is free for 14 days for sales POCs; managed egress addon typical uplift is ~18% on top of base Dedicated pricing. If they want our engineers to run a proxy in their VPC we bill professional services hourly. I'll prepare a ballpark and confirm.

sam: Security wants architecture artifacts if they opt to run their own OCSP proxy. @lee which docs do we need in the questionnaire?

lee: We need: 1) network diagram showing where the proxy lives, 2) IP ranges to allow from our side, 3) cert rotation process for the proxy, and 4) confirmation of logging/retention. If they require us to host an OCSP proxy in their VPC, we need an IP allowlist and IAM role for deployment.

josh: Also check SNI/TLS-inspection interference. Some TLS-inspecting proxies strip SNI or replace it and then the CA responder rejects requests. If `openssl s_client -servername` passes but our runtime fails, collect a `tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/ocsp.pcap tcp and host ocsp.globalca.net` from the host and share. We can run Wireshark on our side to compare.

sam: I'll send the checklist to Acme: `dig`, `curl`, `openssl s_client -status`, `pcap` and whether they have internal mappings for `ocsp.globalca.net`.

security-bot: Security ticket created: SEC-POC-20260221-09 3 - "POC Acme OCSP/DNS split-horizon" assigned to netsec.

elaine: Great. One more note: ask them whether their resolver returns CNAMEs to internal hostnames; that can also route traffic to unreachable subnets. If they can't give outbound to the CA, recommend private deployment + short-term network rule or our managed egress for production.

sam: Thanks all. Looping in Acme and asking for outputs now. Will report back with their dig/curl/pcap files. :white_check_mark:
